 There is already some history between these teams this season. Warren Central opened its campaign with a 20-14 victory over Center Grove on Aug. 21, giving the Warriors an opportunity to complete the season sweep with another win Friday night.
--> There is already some history between these teams this season. Warren Central opened its campaign with a 20-14 victory over Center Grove on Aug. 21, giving the Warriors an opportunity to complete the season sweep with another win Friday night.
 The Warriors have been particularly impressive offensively, averaging 40.9 points and 430.9 total yards per game. Their balanced attack features 204.4 rushing yards and 226.5 passing yards per contest, making them difficult to defend.
--> The Warriors have been particularly impressive offensively, averaging 40.9 points and 430.9 total yards per game. Their balanced attack features 204.4 rushing yards and 226.5 passing yards per contest, making them difficult to defend.
 Running back Keyon Thomas has been a major part of that success, averaging 168.1 rushing yards per game. Quarterback Anthony Dennison provides another dimension, averaging 221.5 passing yards per contest. That combination gives Warren Central plenty of ways to put pressure on opposing defenses.
--> Running back Keyon Thomas has been a major part of that success, averaging 168.1 rushing yards per game. Quarterback Anthony Dennison provides another dimension, averaging 221.5 passing yards per contest. That combination gives Warren Central plenty of ways to put pressure on opposing defenses.
 Center Grove has its own offensive weapons, although the Trojans have leaned more heavily on their ground game. They average 204.5 rushing yards per contest, led by Jayden Biggerstaff, who contributes 89.2 yards per game.
--> Center Grove has its own offensive weapons, although the Trojans have leaned more heavily on their ground game. They average 204.5 rushing yards per contest, led by Jayden Biggerstaff, who contributes 89.2 yards per game.
 Quarterback Oscar Sloan will also be important as Center Grove looks to find opportunities through the air against a Warren Central defense that has allowed 16.5 points per game.

 The Trojans have shown they can be especially dangerous when they get rolling. They have scored 45 points in a shutout victory over Columbus North and previously defeated Whiteland 48-14 to advance through the postseason.

 Warren Central also enters with plenty of momentum after defeating Franklin Central 49-20 in its sectional championship game.
--> Warren Central also enters with plenty of momentum after defeating Franklin Central 49-20 in its sectional championship game.
 The biggest question Friday night might be whether Center Grove can slow down Warren Central's explosive offense while finding enough offensive production to keep pace. The Warriors have averaged more than seven points per game more than the Trojans this season, but their earlier meeting suggests this matchup could be considerably tighter than the numbers indicate.

 Add us as a preferred source on Google Follow Published 1 hour ago | Modified 7 minutes ago KENDALL WEBB Kendall began covering high school sports in East Texas as a high school student in the late 1980s. He served as the sports editor for the Gladewater Mirror early in his career while attending Kilgore College where he received an Associate of Arts with a major in journalism. He later completed his Bachelor of Journalism at The University of Texas at Austin. Webb later founded the College Football America Yearbook, publishing an annual edition every year from 2011 through 2022. Webb added a Master of Liberal Arts with a major in journalism from Harvard University in 2023, simultaneously completing a Graduate Certificate in Digital Storytelling. He has also written for The Sporting News and remains a passionate fan of sports at all levels. He began contributing to High School On SI in 2026.
